newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: Soccer-Keane back in Irish squad, but injured.
newsitem.headline: Soccer-Keane back in Irish squad, but injured.

text.p: Volatile Manchester United midfielder Roy Keane is back in the Irish soccer squad after being left out for the last eight games due to injury, suspension and a rift with manager Mick McCarthy.
McCarthy named Keane in his 20-man squad for the match against Macedonia in Dublin on October 9.
But Keane picked up a leg injury in Manchester United's Champions' League victory over Rapid Vienna on Wednesday and may be ruled out of the Macedonia game.
Keane only made his comeback from a knee injury in Saturday's draw at Aston Villa and the initial verdict is that he will be out of action for a fortnight at least.
Veteran defender Paul McGrath was left out of the Ireland squad, but striker John Aldridge was recalled in place of the injured Niall Quinn.
Aldridge could win his 69th cap against the Macedonians. The 38-year-old striker has so far scored 19 international goals -- just one short of Frank Stapleton's Irish record.
The full Irish squad is as follows,

A Kelly (Sheffield Utd), Given (Blackburn), Irwin (Manchester Utd), Babb (Liverpool), Kenna (Blackburn), Fleming (Middlesbrough), Breen (Birmingham), Harte (Leeds), Cunningham (Wimbledon), Staunton (Aston Villa), Townsend (Aston Villa), Keane (Manchester Utd), Houghton (Crystal Palace), McLoughlin (Portsmouth), McAteer (Liverpool), Moore (Middlesbrough), O'Neill (Norwich), Aldridge (Tranmere), Cascarino (Marseilles), D Kelly (Sunderland).
